observations.summary: The window delegates value-family authority to a machine-readable registry and explicitly keeps the overall buildability gate false.

evidence.quote: `Plans/storage_value_registry.json` is the canonical machine-readable registry for storage value families named in this document.

This Tier 0C-2 registry is partial persistence-materialization progress only. It does not close provider streams, runtime lifecycle, clean-room harness, GUI wiring, security boundary, behavioral acceptance, or broad redb-family blockers; it does not create WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, candidates, executable queues, manifests, implementation files, runtime launches, or product build tasks; and `buildability_gate_passed` remains false.

observations.implication: The window does not itself overclaim product or runtime completion.

observations.summary: Coordination authority is assigned to seglog events and redb projections, while JSON mirrors are explicitly non-authoritative.

evidence.quote: Canonical coordination state is not a JSON file family. It is the `EventRecord` seglog coordination family folded into redb read models with explicit projector checkpoints.

Mirrors cannot drive scheduling, execution admission, conflict prevention, prompt injection, unregister, crash, abort, receipt, or validation decisions. Authoritative consumers use `coordination_snapshot_projection.v1` or the narrower agent/file/operation projections.

observations.implication: Consumers have a clear high-level authority boundary, but its crash and commit semantics still require scrutiny.

observations.summary: The coordination contract combines a 32-agent capacity envelope, caller-supplied idempotency and revision checks, and a redb projection transaction.

evidence.quote: The supported v1 concurrency envelope is up to 32 active agents across multiple worktrees. Above that bound, schedulers must queue, throttle, or require an explicit higher-capacity contract.
Writers provide an idempotency key plus expected `agent_revision` or `last_applied_event_id`; the append and projection result are one logical append/CAS boundary.
The projector advances `coordination_*_projection.v1` rows and `projector.checkpoint.coordination:{project_id}` in one redb transaction.

observations.implication: The high-level concurrency model is present, but several operational decisions remain non-deterministic.

observations.summary: Canonical records are described as immutable lineage-bearing objects while also carrying an update timestamp.

evidence.quote: Canonical records are immutable once committed; corrections require a new record with explicit lineage.
All canonical records include `created_at_utc`, `updated_at_utc`, and `created_by` for audit.

observations.implication: An invariant is needed to prevent update timestamps from being interpreted as permission to mutate canonical rows.

observations.summary: The window defines durable incident lineage, causal coalescing, and user-visible delivery classes.

evidence.quote: Command-originated alerts are durable incident timeline records. Cascade failures use `parent_incident_id` / `parent-incident` bundling so one primary alert owns the `root_cause_key`, child issues attach as related consequences, and CTAs prioritize root-cause repair before derivative failures.
`attention_key` identifies the user-visible attention thread and owning route, while `root_cause_key` identifies the durable causal cluster for `/coalescing`.

Delivery classes are `blocking_modal`, `interruptive_toast`, `persistent_banner_or_card`, and `badge_only`; active-project issues may interrupt when severity requires it, while `non-active-project` issues default to compact global attention until selected.

observations.implication: The ontology is present, but key construction and deterministic delivery selection are not supplied in this window.

observations.summary: Evidence stability, self-containment, legal holds, and export masking are explicitly represented.

evidence.quote: Evidence refs declare exactly one stability class: `embedded_snapshot`, `local_blob_ref`, `external_live_ref`, or `external_missing`.
Exports and history mark a record as not `self-contained` when remote evidence was not snapshotted, including `/exported` views and historical receipt views.

`hold_state` applies to runs, receipts, evidence, blocked episodes, and linked blobs/artifacts; a hold suspends pruning, cleanup, export garbage-collection, and linked-graph deletion until explicitly released.

Local history may keep masked references for joinability, but exports, evidence bundles, and screenshots default to masked values unless the selected export profile explicitly permits fuller disclosure.

observations.implication: The storage vocabulary supports privacy-aware evidence handling, but authority and lifecycle transitions need further specification.

observations.summary: The window distinguishes active and focused runs, preserves historical focus across navigation, and gates actions on freshness and health.

evidence.quote: Project state stores `active_run_id`, `focused_run_id`, and `focus_mode = live | historical` so live dashboards, historical inspectors, and restart rehydration all resolve the same focused run.
Cross-tab deep links and search pivots MUST target the focused run context; switching tabs or reopening the app does not silently retarget links back to the active run when `focus_mode = historical`.

Sensitive action gating evaluates both axes together: stale-but-healthy projections can require refresh, degraded projections can fall back to canonical record reads, and unavailable projections block projection-dependent actions.

observations.implication: Read-context truth is addressed, while mutation-target truth in historical mode remains unresolved.

observations.summary: The window requires versioned migration, startup projection recomputation, and explicit retention anchors.

evidence.quote: Migrations are versioned and idempotent; old schema versions must be supported for at least one major release.
Projection freshness is tracked per projection type; stale projections are recomputed at startup.

Retention policies for receipts, log tails, watch buffers, explorer snapshots, and stale caches MUST store both `retention_anchor_kind` and `retention_anchor_at_utc`; implementations MUST NOT infer the anchor from file mtime alone.

observations.implication: These are useful baselines, but the operational bounds and release authority are not fully defined within the capsule.

Commit ordering, acknowledgement, and recovery when the seglog append succeeds but the redb transaction fails are not defined.

Migrations are versioned and idempotent; old schema versions must be supported for at least one major release.
Projection freshness is tracked per projection type; stale projections are recomputed at startup.
Exports and history mark a record as not `self-contained` when remote evidence was not snapshotted, including `/exported` views and historical receipt views.
`attention_key` identifies the user-visible attention thread and owning route, while `root_cause_key` identifies the durable causal cluster for `/coalescing`.
Repeated events with the same `root_cause_key` update one active alert thread; interruptive notifications retrigger only on severity or state transition.

Delivery classes are `blocking_modal`, `interruptive_toast`, `persistent_banner_or_card`, and `badge_only`; active-project issues may interrupt when severity requires it, while `non-active-project` issues default to compact global attention until selected.

Command-originated alerts are durable incident timeline records. Cascade failures use `parent_incident_id` / `parent-incident` bundling so one primary alert owns the `root_cause_key`, child issues attach as related consequences, and CTAs prioritize root-cause repair before derivative failures.
`base-branch` ownership must be reconciled before Source Control or UI code mint competing base-branch fields.

Required alert timeline fields are `raised_at`, `source_surface`, `severity`, `root_cause_key`, `owning_surface`, `acknowledged/snoozed state`, `resolved_at`, and linked receipt/run/worktree/workflow/container/workload ids (`receipt_id`, `run_id`, `worktree_id`, `workflow_run_id`, `container_id`, `workload_id`).
